analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds changelog.d/qwen-gdn-prompt-kernel.md (lines 1-4), a paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 595-611) and one row in docs/reference/configuration.md (line 414). All three describe a four-row Gated DeltaNet prompt-prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. A per-process GPU probe keeps the packed or rows kernel only if it reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit; otherwise the stock kernel runs. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and windows shorter than 16 positions always use the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED is a process-local env var. Its values 0/false/no/off keep the stock kernel. packed or rows force that kernel and skip the parity check. The docs say it is read once per process and not forwarded to LaunchAgents. No code, wire contract, attestation, key, authorization or cache-storage control is changed, so I found no security regression.

Relevant threats: T-041 and TB-007. The docs claim that bit-exactness keeps the recurrent state used by prefix-cache checkpoint capture unchanged. The SSD cache keys carry no kernel identity, so a numerical divergence would mix checkpoints across kernels. That would be a correctness or integrity risk, not a new confidentiality channel. The probe window is fixed, so no tenant data is involved. The faster prefill shifts TTFT timing, but that is the same kind as the accepted SEC-035 oracle. The env override is operator-controlled, and the operator is already ADV-001 with full local control (TB-003), so it adds no privilege or remote surface.

Unverified contract: GatedDelta.swift (GatedDeltaPrefill) is not in the supplied evidence. The soundness of the probe, its coverage of all dtypes and geometries, and whether a forced kernel could corrupt checkpointed state cannot be confirmed from the docs. A later pass should review that code if it is part of the PR.
